Why Botswana?

1

Stable economy & governance

2

Skilled, English-speaking workforce

Well-educated talent across sectors, from technology to customer service.

3

Competitive labour costs cut operating expenses without compromising quality.

4

5

6

7

UK-based legal system

Familiar legal foundations make contracts and other legal work straightforward.

About Victus Global

Africa can become a globally recognised food production powerhouse.

We are a group of companies committed to transforming agriculture and empowering women in Africa — developing the continent in a sustainable way that benefits all.

Our story

Built on dignity, respect and a passion for Africa

Our ethos is to empower farmers and SMEs with the expertise to grow their businesses and benefit from socio-economic empowerment. We start with the local markets growing fastest — where companies can gain an advantage in cost, product or route to market — and take a partnership approach that aligns producers with consumers.

2012

Victus Global Ltd

Founded by Bo Masole as a food security consultancy, developing and mentoring food manufacturers and primary producers in Africa to compete and sell locally, regionally and in European and UK markets.

2016

Victus Global Capital Ltd

Founded by Zee de Gersigny and Bo Masole to direct investment to food manufacturers and primary producers who need capital to reach the next level.

2017

US$50m women-led agribusiness fund

Launched in partnership with Altree Capital to invest in women-led agribusinesses across Africa.

How we deliver

A proven four-stage project model

We make sure we know where products will be sold before production begins.

STAGE 01

Strategic planning

  • Sub-sector market review and competitor benchmarking
  • Country standards and legislation
  • Market, seasonality and supply-chain analysis
  • Securing strategic buying partners

STAGE 02

Pilot project

  • Select local farmers or manufacturers
  • Assemble experts from our associate network
  • Develop standards for target markets
  • Train, mentor and share knowledge

STAGE 03

Project development

  • National roll-out to processors, farmers and start-ups
  • Technical assistance and ongoing mentoring
  • Supply-chain education
  • Operational and production support

STAGE 04

Evaluation review

  • Evaluation criteria set up front
  • Market penetration, volume and value
  • Rate of sale, consumer trends, distribution
  • Mid-term and final evaluations

Project experience

Selected work across Africa, Europe and beyond

Zambia · since 2012

UNIDO–WTO trade capacity building

Zambian suppliers struggled with retailer requirements, a challenging supply chain and gaps in food safety knowledge — leaving retailers unable to source locally. Using the GFSI Global Markets Programme’s three-phase approach, we mentor suppliers towards internationally recognised certification and train local experts to build lasting capacity.

10 COMESA member states

COMESA GFSI Global Markets capacity building

A voluntary scheme to raise SPS, technical and quality-management standards for SMEs in Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe — from design and pilot to full scale, supported by an online platform for training, SOPs and certification guidance, and aligned with AfCFTA goals.

Zambia

Zambeef PLC

Implementing a functional Food Safety Management System with one of Zambia’s largest integrated agri-businesses, delivering improved quality and greater market access.

Ethiopia & Angola

Unilever regulatory scan

An in-depth investigative mission with government institutions, parastatals and private organisations covering gazetted and non-gazetted import rules for FMCG — resulting in Unilever commissioning a homecare plant in Ethiopia.

UK, Europe & South America

Nomad Foods (Iglo)

Auditing raw-material suppliers across Europe and worldwide for Europe’s leading branded frozen food business, home of Birds Eye, Iglo and Findus.
